note: s + consonant takes LO, never IL. Her rule on the tape: «perché la parola comincia con SP».
sp- → lo.
st- → lo.
ps- counts too — the test is s+consonant, not the letter s alone.
Even a borrowed word obeys it: lo standard, lo sport, lo staff.
z- takes LO as well — from «prodotti con molto zucchero».
sedersi. And alla = a + la — Day 1's rule, still working.

it: mi preparo per la lezione di italiano
en: I get ready for the Italian lesson
note: prepararsi. She noted mi preparo has no clean English equivalent.
alzarsi, third person: si alza. alle for the hour — Day 1.

en: are you getting your hair cut?
note: tagliarsi. Reflexive because it is YOUR hair — Italian marks that, English doesn't.

it: quando sei a Napoli ti siedi al bar o sei in piedi?
en: when you're in Naples do you sit at the bar or stand?
note: in piedi = standing. The everyday Neapolitan question.

it: noi ci sediamo al bar e beviamo un caffè
en: we sit at the bar and drink a coffee
note: ci sediamo — first person plural. The pronoun still comes first.
su + il = sul. Another fused preposition.
Reciprocal: the -si means one another, not oneself.

it: mi incontro con amici a Napoli
en: I meet up with friends in Naples
note: mi incontro CON — the preposition stays.

it: noi ci incontriamo in centro a Napoli
en: we meet in the centre of Naples
note: ci incontriamo — reciprocal plural. in centro, no article.

en: to deal with, to look after
note: Takes DI: occuparsi di qualcosa.

it: lei si occupa di appartamenti per i militari
en: she handles apartments for the military
note: si occupa DI — never occuparsi a/con.
Day 1's sign-off, still the standard.
sentirsi = to hear one another. Use it when the next contact is by phone or message.
ricordare + direct object — no pronoun needed.
ricordarsi, standing alone. Both forms are correct; the reflexive is more colloquial.
The double negative is REQUIRED: non … niente.

it: non ricordo di prendere le medicine
en: I don't remember to take the medicine
note: Before a verb it needs DI: ricordare DI + infinito. Her note: «non ricordo + di + prendere».
The one to have ready in every lesson.
Softer than non capisco — you're following the person, not the words.
Imperative with the pronoun ATTACHED — the opposite of the present tense.
CONOSCERE for places and people; SAPERE for facts. See the correction below.
Ghedi, Aviano.
Feminine: l'aviazione.
quotidiano = daily — what she is actually teaching you.
il neurone → i neuroni.

en: products with a lot of sugar
note: molto agrees with nothing here — it modifies zucchero.
Unchanged since Day 1.
